code_snippet:
# Kafka Producer Exactly-Once Semantics Configuration
enable.idempotence=true
acks=all
retries=2147483647
max.in.flight.requests.per.connection=5

content.tldr: Exactly-Once Semantics (EOS) during production is achieved by enabling producer idempotence (`enable.idempotence=true`) and transactional two-phase commit across partitions.
content.simple_explanation: Network timeouts during production can cause duplicate messages if a broker writes a record but its ACK is lost in transit, prompting the producer to retry. Enabling idempotence assigns the producer a unique 64-bit Producer ID (PID) and a monotonically increasing sequence number per partition. The broker verifies incoming sequence numbers, transparently deduplicating retried records. For multi-partition atomic writes, Kafka Transactions use a two-phase commit coordinator.
content.real_world_example: A financial wire transfer with transaction reference IDs: if the internet disconnects after submitting transfer #1042, re-submitting transfer #1042 allows the bank to recognize the duplicate ID and ensure your account is only debited once.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: End-to-end exactly-once processing requires both idempotent production and transactional consumption (`isolation.level=read_committed`) to prevent reading uncommitted transaction aborts.
